answers.brief_reasoning: Take the last digit with n % 10 and add it to the sum, then drop it with n /= 10. Repeat while n > 0. If n is 0 the loop never runs, so the method returns 0.

Start at start and count upward. Return the first number that its digitSum divides evenly. Because start >= 1, every digit sum is at least 1, so there is no division by zero. The loop always ends because 10 is a Harshad number, so one is always reached.
